## finalfantasy.fandom.com (Information; Final Fantasy Wiki, mirror breezewiki.com)

- https://breezewiki.com/finalfantasy/wiki/Crystal_Defenders -- accessed 2026-10-20 (page text pasted by user)
  - Crystal Defenders (クリスタル・ディフェンダーズ, Kurisutaru Difendāzu), originally released in Japan as Crystal Guardians: developer Tose, publisher Square Enix, a defense simulation, single player, PEGI 7+; a defensive strategy game with jobs from Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift; 12 stages across three versions W1, W2 and W3 (the Wii versions R1 and R2)
  - The remake Crystal Defenders +Plus (クリスタル・ディフェンダーズ Plus, Kurisutaru Difendāzu Plus) came to iOS and iPadOS with similar content, smoother play and downloadable maps
  - The page's Versions section (https://breezewiki.com/finalfantasy/wiki/Crystal_Defenders#Versions, pasted by user 2026-10-20), by platform:
    - Mobile phone: released in Japan as Crystal Guardians, in episodes W1, W2 and W3; the feature phone services in Japan ended 2018-03-31 (JST) with the other Square Enix Mobile titles
    - Xbox Games Store: 800 MS Points, W1 to W3 in full, twelve achievements for 200 gamerscore, like all XBLA games
    - PSN: W1 to W3, with a free demo of a 20-wave stage from W1 (Soldier, Black Mage and Archer jobs)
    - iPod: a separate version for the iPod Nano and Classic, played with the click wheel, with W1 and W2 only, much harder than the WiiWare version
    - iOS: W1 to W3 with touch controls, four maps per chapter (12 in all, 30 waves each), a full version and a Lite version (one map, 20 waves of W1); the upgrade Crystal Defenders +Plus has the same content with better graphics and smoother play, free to download with the free stage Bisga Greenlands and paid packs for the rest, DLC maps planned
    - WiiWare: two installments, R1 (the first 12 stages plus a bonus stage for a perfect run, played with the Wii Remote held sideways) and R2; much easier than the iPod version
    - Android: W1 and W2 only; available on Google Play and the Amazon Appstore
  - Release dates: iOS (iPhone and iPod touch) 2008-12-23 and iPad 2010-07-01, Android 2011-01-25 (all regions); Xbox 360 2009-03-11 (Japan, United States, Europe) and Xbox One 2016-07-21; WiiWare United States 2009-04-20; PlayStation 3 Japan 2009-03-11 and Europe 2009-07-23; PSP 2009-10-29
  - Closures: iOS 2016-05-31 (end of life), Wii 2019-01-30, Android and Fire OS summer 2019; the PlayStation 3, PSP and Xbox 360 offline versions remain available
  - The entry's date 2008-01-28 predates all of these (the Japanese mobile phone release as Crystal Guardians)

## ja.wikipedia.org (Information)

- https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/クリスタル_ガーディアンズ -- accessed 2026-10-20 (read by me through the MediaWiki API; found while checking the W1 and W3 dates the user asked about)
  - Crystal Guardians (クリスタル ガーディアンズ), a defense-simulation tower defense game by Square Enix, 1 player, developer MSF/Wings; the mobile versions came first, as three apps by difficulty through "Final Fantasy Mobile" (platforms i-appli, S!appli and EZappli (BREW)): **W1 2008-01-28, W2 2008-03-10, W3 2008-05-08**; the compilation Crystal Defenders (W1 to W3; the iPod and Android versions only W1 and W2) followed for consoles and other platforms
  - The entry's `titleDate` is the range of the mobile episodes, 2008-01-28 to 2008-05-08 (user's idea, 2026-10-20), as the serialization rule for a run of releases
  - Later dates on the page (Japan): iPod and iPhone 2008-12-23, Wii R1 2009-01-27 and R2 2009-02-24, Xbox 360 and PS3 2009-03-11, PSP 2009-10-29, iPad 2010-07-01, Android listed as 2011-12-01 (the date Square Enix Market gives for its Android version; the official Japanese page says 2011-01-26); the iPhone version's interface was panned in Japan and a landscape-control update followed in April 2009
  - Its infobox lists Wii (WiiWare) among the platforms, with R1 on 2009-01-27 and R2 on 2009-02-24 in Japan; the text says the WiiWare version is not the W series but a new series on other maps, R1 and R2 (R1 doubles as a tutorial for beginners; a Moogle youth gathers companions to protect the crystals); so the Edit's languages start with Japanese as native (user, 2026-10-20)
  - The page also has a section on Vanguard Storm (see the crystal-defenders-vanguard-storm source)

## Is it still playable? (checked 2026-10-20)

- Yes, so the entry is not terminated (user's rule: a game that is still playable or purchasable is not terminated; the struck rows are the versions that closed)
  - The Xbox store page https://www.xbox.com/en-US/games/store/crystal-defenders/BVCHVG7HM8LG (fetched by me today, HTTP 200) is titled "Buy CRYSTAL DEFENDERS | XBOX" and its data lists the game as in stock for Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S with a purchase action and a price
  - Confirmed by the user (2026-10-20): the en-CA page (https://www.xbox.com/en-CA/games/store/crystal-defenders/BVCHVG7HM8LG) showed no Buy button in a normal browser window but did show it in a private window, so the game can be bought (the missing button in the signed-in browser is account- or session-specific, and the page data says in stock with a purchase action in en-US, en-CA, en-GB and ja-JP)
  - The official Japanese game page (live) says the game can still be bought on the Microsoft Store as an Xbox backward-compatible game; the Final Fantasy Wiki says the PS3, PSP and Xbox 360 offline versions remain available; Final Fantasy Union (2019-08-06) says the Xbox 360, PSP (playable on Vita) and PS3 versions were the only ones left
  - A Reddit comment by Psyk60 (https://www.reddit.com/r/FinalFantasy/comments/12ftqf2/crystal_defenders/jfh4hed/, pasted by user 2026-10-20, written about three years earlier, around April 2023): it is still available on the Xbox store, being on the list of backwards compatible games so it works on an Xbox One or Series; it might still be available on the PS3 store, which can only be reached with a PS3; and "Yes it's on Vita too" (the PSP game on the Vita store), checked on the commenter's own Vita
  - So as of about 2023 the Vita store (the PSP version) sold it and the PS3 store probably did; whether they still do today is not verified (their web store pages are gone), so the PS3, PSP and Vita rows are not struck

  - Page URL by capture: 2013-06-11 to 2017-10-10 http://www.jp.square-enix.com/game/android/ (the per-model page, titled Android); 2018-06-27 http://www.jp.square-enix.com/game/pf/android/ (the per-model page, titled Android | ゲーム; the saved page lists 76 items and a もっと見る button); 2019-03-09 to live (2026-10-27) https://www.jp.square-enix.com/game/ with the model filter set to Android, platform filter ?pf=12 (the saved pages show the model checkbox value 12 checked; the pages' own address is https://www.jp.square-enix.com/game/); each capture is https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>/<page URL>, timestamps listed in sources/final-fantasy-franchise.md
  - Icons: 2013-06-11 to 2017-10-10 the icon image ダウンロード専用 (download only) on items; from 2018-06-27 the model label image Android (the model, not repeated below) and the label ダウンロード on items, the store buttons Google Playでダウンロード or SQUARE ENIX MARKETでダウンロード (2018) or Google Play or SQUARE ENIX MARKET (2019 on) beside 購入する (2019 on), and 事前登録する (2018) or 事前登録 (2019 on) on items not yet out; the ダウンロード専用 image and the ダウンロード label are both written ダウンロード below, 事前登録する and 事前登録 both 事前登録, the store buttons are written Google Play and SQUARE ENIX MARKET. Date label: 発売日 (release) or 配信日 (delivery), by item. CERO: no rating label on any capture
  - Link labels: 公式サイト (official site), 商品詳細 (detail page, 2019 on), Google Play and SQUARE ENIX MARKET (the store pages); 2013 to 2017 the thumbnail image links to the same page as the first link; a link's archived URL is the capture of the link as the saved page renders it (the first, and the last when different); links of the live page have no archive
  - クリスタル・ディフェンダーズ; ディフェンス・シミュレーション; first listed 2013-06-11: release 2011.01.25; icons: ダウンロード; changes: 2017-10-10: release 2011.01.25 to 2011.01.26 / 2019-03-09: genre ディフェンス・シミュレーション to ディフェンス・シミュレーション ※スマホ版配信終了; listed in every capture from 2013-06-11 to live (2026-10-27) except 2018-06-27
    - http://www.crystaldefenders.jp/jp/ -- 公式サイト link, listed 2013-06-11 to 2017-10-10 -- link recorded only -- archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20130611124444/http://www.crystaldefenders.jp/jp/ (last listing: https://web.archive.org/web/20171010160332/http://www.crystaldefenders.jp/jp/)

## Decisions
- No `by` line (user, 2026-10-20): Ryoma Ito (illustrations) is named by the Crystal Defenders Plus site and Gamicus, but the entry carries no credits
- Split into versions (user, 2026-10-20): the primary is the original W series (no subtitle; W1 to W3: mobile, iOS, iPad, Android, Xbox 360, PS3, PSP; the iPad app stays here), with the iOS Plus as the Remake (2013) and the WiiWare R series as the Edit (2009) in versions[]; the primary keeps the ratings; the languages are the combined list of the Apple listings (the iPhone, iPad and Plus pages all list English, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese and Spanish, checked in the captures); the Edit's languages are from the Nintendo pages (see nintendo.com); the Remake row has no suffix, its subtitle says it
